name: Califone
label: Thrill Jockey
lede: What was left of Red Red Meat went looking through the junk drawer of American music, and came back with bottles, hand drums, tape hiss and a heron-headed god from Tim Rutili's dreams.

eras.title: Red Red Meat, and what it cost
eras.text: Before Califone there was Red Red Meat, Tim Rutili's Chicago blues-rock band on Sub Pop. It toured with the Smashing Pumpkins, lost bassist Glynis Johnson to AIDS, and slowly turned stranger with every record. By 1997 it had run its course, and most of its people would follow Rutili into the next thing.

years.h: Friends of Betty becomes Red Red Meat
years.p: Tim Rutili's Chicago band, which had included Ben Massarella, renames itself [[Red Red Meat|d2952878-d32a-4e09-b6c8-6f9598e5cfbe]] after recruiting Glenn Girard. Glynis Johnson, Rutili's partner since his film-school days, is on bass.

years.h: Engineer Brian Deck sits down at the drums
years.p: Red Red Meat cut its first single, Hot Nikkety Trunk Monkey, at Idful Studios with [[Brad Wood|58c8c056-4f9a-4a3b-8dd9-69b06bb23c28]]. Idful co-founder [[Brian Deck|e91d5dc5-12a7-45cf-af2b-f120def0f711]] becomes the band's full-time drummer.

years.src: Wikipedia: Red Red Meat · Wikipedia: Tim Rutili
years.h: Glynis Johnson dies of AIDS-related complications
years.p: After Red Red Meat's summer 1992 tour with the [[Smashing Pumpkins|ba0d6274-db14-4ef5-b28d-657ebde1a396]], bassist Glynis Johnson leaves the band. According to Wikipedia she died that fall of AIDS-related complications; she and Tim Rutili had been together for years.

years.h: Jimmywine Majestic · Red Red Meat on Sub Pop
years.p: Red Red Meat's Sub Pop album brings Ben Massarella back, banging on percussion next to Brian Deck's drum kit. The two-drummer clatter becomes a Califone trademark.

years.h: There's a Star Above the Manger Tonight, the last Red Red Meat LP
years.p: Red Red Meat's final Sub Pop album closes the book. After it the band effectively stops, and Tim Rutili starts recording alone at home.

eras.title: Little pop songs out of found pieces
eras.text: Califone began as a Tim Rutili home project named after a maker of school record players. Red Red Meat's blues stayed, but everything else was up for grabs: old folk, electronics, Psychic TV, silent movies. Friends from Chicago drifted in until it was a band.

q: Now it seems like just about anything goes.
years.h: Tim Rutili starts Califone as a solo home project
years.p: Tim Rutili sets out to make little pop songs out of found pieces, and names the project after Califone International, the audio equipment maker.
years.xp:
Red Red Meat had a sound people expected. Califone, Rutili said, didn't: it started as a bedroom experiment, tape loops and junk-shop instruments stitched into songs, and only slowly became a group with rotating players from Red Red Meat and other Chicago bands.

The name comes from Califone International, the company whose sturdy record players filled American classrooms.

years.h: Califone's first EP comes out on Flydaddy
years.p: Tim Rutili makes the debut Califone EP with Red Red Meat's Tim Hurley, released by Flydaddy Records.

years.h: Roomsound, Califone's first full album, on Perishable
years.p: Califone's first proper album comes out on Chicago's Perishable Records. Dead Oceans reissued Roomsound with extras in 2016.

years.h: Ugly Casanova: Tim Rutili teams with Modest Mouse's Isaac Brock
years.p: Tim Rutili, Ben Massarella and Brian Deck join [[Isaac Brock|071d3d16-8ed7-4e06-be96-2c52defcf434]] of [[Modest Mouse|a96ac800-bfcb-412a-8a63-0a98df600700]] in [[Ugly Casanova|5c2d7596-2366-47c5-b4a2-0550ac8f9e69]] for Sharpen Your Teeth on Sub Pop. Deck produces and drums.

years.h: Deceleration One: Califone scores silent films live
years.p: Califone had been playing live soundtracks to silent-era films. Deceleration One collects the instrumental results; Deceleration Two followed in 2003, and parts three and four were talked about but never came out.

eras.title: Bottles, hand drums and the heron king
eras.text: On Thrill Jockey, Califone made the three records that defined it. Songs were built from improvised jams, then dressed with lyrics, loops and junk percussion. The Chicago Tribune and the New York Times started paying attention, and the band spent long stretches on the road in Europe and the US.

years.h: Quicksand/Cradlesnakes · Califone's first Thrill Jockey LP
years.p: Califone moves to Thrill Jockey with Quicksand/Cradlesnakes, the start of a three-album run on the Chicago label.

years.h: Heron King Blues, built from Tim Rutili's bird dreams
years.p: Califone improvised the basic tracks of Heron King Blues in three days at a studio on Chicago's South Side. The 15-minute title track is named for a Druid god Tim Rutili kept seeing in a recurring dream.
years.xp:
Rutili had dreamed all his life of a giant man-bird, and had a real fear of birds. He later matched the figure to the heron king of Druid lore: an effigy that, the legend goes, sent British soldiers running when it was raised.

The band wrote nothing in advance. Taking [[Captain Beefheart|a1594afa-2f6b-4596-a156-a35853dca691]]'s Mirror Man as a model, Ben Massarella and Joe Adamik on percussion and Jim Becker on everything else jammed until the grooves held, then added words, steel guitar, bottles, hand drums and loops. Trick Bird was co-written with members of Orso.

years.h: Chicago Tribune names Heron King Blues 2004's best local indie album
years.p: The Chicago Tribune ranks Califone's Heron King Blues the best Chicago indie album of 2004.

years.h: Califone backs Freakwater on Thinking of You
years.p: Califone serves as the backing band on [[Freakwater|50e68a47-b6e4-4178-84d5-8955206a0b7f]]'s Thinking of You, another Thrill Jockey record.

years.h: Califone music lands in Stranger than Fiction
years.p: Califone contributes to the soundtrack of the 2006 film Stranger than Fiction, and starts staging animation-and-live-music pieces with filmmaker Brent Green.

years.h: Roots & Crowns · thrill 163
years.p: Recorded between October 2005 and May 2006, Roots & Crowns includes The Orchids, a [[Psychic TV|14c5a3a3-f5ed-4978-99af-486010e3a007]] cover. Pitchfork gave it 8.7 and later put it at No. 168 on its list of the 2000s' best albums.

eras.title: A ghost story with a band attached
eras.text: Tim Rutili turned Califone into a film project: an album and a feature with the same name, which went to Sundance and then on tour with the band playing its soundtrack live. The band moved to Dead Oceans, and Red Red Meat played one last time.

years.h: Califone backs Flecton on The Bright Side of Dying
years.p: Ottawa's Flecton releases The Bright Side of Dying on Kelp Records with Tim Rutili, Ben Massarella, Joe Adamik and Jim Becker as its band. The eight-song vinyl includes a [[Merle Haggard|deb2448c-6fdf-4d31-921e-757630515dbd]] cover.

years.h: Califone signs to Dead Oceans
years.p: Pitchfork reports Califone's move from Thrill Jockey to Dead Oceans on July 7, 2009.

years.h: Red Red Meat plays a final show at Millennium Park
years.p: [[Red Red Meat|d2952878-d32a-4e09-b6c8-6f9598e5cfbe]], reunited for a handful of shows in 2008 and 2009, plays what was billed as its final show at Chicago's Millennium Park.

years.h: All My Friends Are Funeral Singers: the album
years.p: Califone's first Dead Oceans record doubles as the score for Tim Rutili's feature film of the same name.
play: All My Friends Are Funeral Singers

years.h: Tim Rutili's film All My Friends Are Funeral Singers goes to Sundance
years.p: Tim Rutili wrote and directed the film: a psychic woman lives alone in the woods with ghosts she must set free. It was accepted to the 2010 Sundance Film Festival, and Califone toured playing the soundtrack live under the screen.
years.xp:
Rutili described the premise simply: the woman has to find a way to release the spirits that are wrecking her life. The film starred Angela Bettis, Rutili's wife.

Instead of a normal album tour, Califone took the movie on the road and played the record as its live score.

years.h: Made a Machine by Describing the Landscape: the Califone film
years.p: IndiePix releases a feature documentary by Solan Jensen and Joshua Marie Wilkinson, following Califone on European and US tours after Heron King Blues.

years.h: Califone players help make Iron & Wine's Kiss Each Other Clean
years.p: Califone members play on [[Iron & Wine|c3f28da8-662d-4f09-bdc7-3084bf685930]]'s Kiss Each Other Clean. Brian Deck had produced earlier Iron & Wine records.

eras.title: Every song its own planet
eras.text: After a quiet spell, Tim Rutili came back writing more personally, recording away from Chicago and working with different players on every song. Califone kept going on small labels, house-concert tours and film scores, with Ben Massarella and Rachel Blumberg still at Rutili's side.

years.h: Stitches, recorded across California, Arizona and Texas
years.p: Tim Rutili left his usual Chicago base and made Stitches across Southern California, Arizona and Texas, treating each song as its own planet with different musicians.
years.xp: Dead Oceans' notes describe garage-sale drum machines, slack guitar strings and hushed vocals next to brass, pedal steel, strings and tablas. Rutili said he forced himself to write as much as possible and to let himself be crabby and vulnerable.

years.h: Funeral Singers lands in the Watch Dogs video game
years.p: Califone's Funeral Singers appears on the soundtrack of Ubisoft's Watch Dogs.

years.h: Guitars Tuned to Air Conditioners on Jealous Butcher
years.p: Califone's move to Portland's Jealous Butcher Records follows the Insect Courage EP in March and a Dead Oceans reissue of Roomsound.

years.h: Califone plays living rooms: a house-concert tour
years.p: Tim Rutili, Ben Massarella and percussionist Rachel Blumberg, a former [[The Decemberists|97b1142f-c71e-4971-8736-4a8ceaf6b4c3]] drummer, tour house concerts and small rooms as a trio.

years.h: Echo Mine · Jealous Butcher
years.p: Califone's Echo Mine comes out on Jealous Butcher Records.

years.h: Villagers · Jealous Butcher
years.p: Califone's Villagers arrives on Jealous Butcher, and gets a companion record two years later.

years.h: The Villager's Companion, released on Valentine's Day
years.p: Califone's nine-song follow-up to Villagers opens with Every Amnesia Movie and closes with Crazy as a Loon.
